Subject: Next steps & procurement path \u0014 Redwood evaluation (PO vs Card / Marketplace)

Hi Jordan / Kelly \u0014

Great to meet today \u0014 thanks for walking us through the latency and security requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Recap from discovery: primary use is product-facing chat with strict PII retention controls, target 99th p95 latency < 180ms, and monthly committed throughput ~120M tokens.
- Procurement path options we discussed: (1) Card for pilot/POC, (2) Purchase Order + Master Services Agreement for enterprise commit, or (3) AWS Marketplace listing if you need procurement via your marketplace catalog.

Next steps:
1) I attached our latest SOC 2 report and a draft SOW to start procurement review (see attachments).
2) Can you confirm whether Acme prefers a PO or card for initial payment? If PO, please share your standard PO template and estimated approval timeline.
3) Vivek will send a short tech appendix (KV cache, data isolation notes) by Monday.

If easier, happy to loop in your procurement contact directly \u0014 adding Ben on cc who can coordinate contract terms and discounts for annual commits.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: SOC2_report_2025.pdf, SOW_Redwood-Acme_v1.docx

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecorp.com>

Cc: procurement@acmecorp.com, Kelly Tran <kelly.tran@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Apr 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps & procurement path \u0014 Redwood evaluation (PO vs Card / Marketplace)

Thanks Marissa \u0014

Appreciate the recap and the SOC2 doc. A few quick notes from procurement:

- For the pilot, Acme usually prefers card payments or a short-term invoice rather than a full PO, unless there's a commitment > $50k. The pilot budget is $8k\u001012k, so card would be simplest.
- If we move to production and commit to 12 months, procurement will require an MSA + PO. Typical internal approval takes 3\u00134 weeks once legal signs off.
- We are also evaluating AWS Marketplace for platform purchases; that route would require Redwood to be listed. Is Redwood on AWS Marketplace now or is that upcoming?

I'll check with procurement and get back on the PO template if we end up going that route. For now card looks easiest for the POC.

Best,
Jordan
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecorp.com>, Kelly Tran <kelly.tran@acmecorp.com>

Date: Mon, 06 Apr 2026 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps & procurement path \u0014 Redwood evaluation (PO vs Card / Marketplace)

Thanks Jordan \u0014 that's helpful. Short answers:

- Card payment works fine for the pilot \u0014 we can spin up a short-term subscription and invoice card.
- For production contracts (MSA + PO) Ben will lead on commercial terms and can share a standard order form.
- Redwood is in the late stages of AWS Marketplace onboarding; we do have a private listing partner flow but a public listing is expected Q3. If Marketplace is a blocker, Ben can coordinate a reseller flow or we can do a direct PO.

I'll have Vivek share the tech appendix today and Ben will follow up with our commercial templates and typical timelines.

Two asks for you: 1) Can you confirm who in procurement I should follow up with (name + email)? 2) Any required vendor compliance docs beyond SOC2 (e.g., data processing agreement, ISO, background checks)?

Thanks \u0014
Marissa
